sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2001 Renault Clio V6, finished in Iceberg Silver with a blue and gray interior, and will be displayed live at Willow Springs Reimagined as part of the Cars & Bids Willow Springs Collection. This Renault is a Japanese-market, left-hand-drive hatchback currently titled in Washington state and located in California. Badged the "Lutécia V6" for the Japanese market, this Clio V6 is equipped with a metric instrument cluster, and the odometer currently displays approximately 30,300 kilometers, or approximately 19,000 miles. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the selling dealer includes 17-inch wheels, a Clio V6-specific body kit, leather and synthetic suede upholstery, front sport seats, and a CD player. The selling dealer reports no notable modifications. Born from the Clio V6 Trophy race car, the road-going Renault Clio V6 arrived in 2001 as one of Renault Sport's most ambitious creations. For the "Phase 1" Clio V6, TWR transformed the humble front-engine, front-wheel-drive Clio into a wide-bodied, mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive two-seater, with each example hand-built in Uddevalla, Sweden. Its exotic layout, dramatic proportions, and famously demanding handling made it unlike virtually anything else on sale -- and its appearances in mid-'00s media like Top Gear, Need for Speed, and plenty more helped establish the Clio V6 as a modern Renault icon even in parts of the world where it was never originally sold. Power comes from a 3.0-liter V6, rated at 230 horsepower and 221 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
